articles.summary: Updates from the Great Barrier Reef Arena. Start time in Mackay is 10am AEST. Any thoughts? Email Megan. 43rd over: Australia 183-8 (Green 64, Lyon 15) Hasan continues his spell and he picks up where he left off with his line and length targeting the stumps.
body: 47th over: Australia 186-8 (Green 67, Lyon 15) Taijul continues and Lyon has fielders crowding around the bat and being very vocal, but Lyon doesn’t seem bothered, blocking out the over and not breaking a sweat.

46th over: Australia 186-8 (Green 67, Lyon 15) Shoriful starts his next over with a bouncer. Green then finds an opportunity for his pull shot and they run hard to get two. Those are the only runs from the over as Shoriful tightens the screws.

45th over: Australia 184-8 (Green 65, Lyon 15) After that loose over from Hasan, we have Taijul Islam coming into the attack with his left arm orthodox. Green defends the first ball, then rotates the strike to give Lyon a look at his fellow spinner. Just the one run from the over.

44th over: Australia 183-8 (Green 64, Lyon 15) Shoriful resumes and Lyon starts the over defensively. Shoriful throws in a bouncer and then strikes the thigh pad and appeals for LBW, but the umpire isn’t interested and Bangaldesh eventually decide that it’s probably too high to bother reviewing. A maiden from Shoriful.

articles.title: José Mourinho marks Real Madrid return with late drama and touch of humility | Sid Lowe
articles.summary: The old master is back at Madrid as he begins with celebrations, frustrations and finally relief at Espanyol. José Mourinho says he is calmer now so when the rest of the bench emptied, sprinting down the touchline to celebrate the 90th-minute goal that finally delivered victory on his first game in…
body: For all those stars; for all that Mourinho’s main task might just have been been to find a way to fit Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham together; for all that he had introduced Yan Diomande, the most expensive player in the club’s history, it was a 21-year-old, unknown six months ago and unexpectedly signed from Levante, who got the goal that secured victory upon the coach’s second coming.

Espí, whose goals had rescued Levante from relegation last season and who is still living at Madrid’s Valdebebas training ground like his coach, the two of them sharing breakfast every morning, was signed for pretty much this: to be a different type of striker, an old-school No 9, with a presence in the area. And when a scrappy, broken-up move ended with Mbappé seeing the ball run away from him in the area, there he was to force it over the line. Perhaps even to pose a question: is his a profile they could do with and not just in reserve? This time, at least, it had worked.

articles.title: Arthur Fils blasts past Flavio Cobolli to reach first Masters final in landmark win
articles.summary: French youngster beats No 7 seed 6-3, 6-4 in Cincinnati. Jessica Pegula battles past Swiatek to reach women’s final. In the middle of a tense, erratic start to a rain-delayed semi-final day in Cincinnati, Arthur Fils found himself locked in defence and miles behind the baseline on his serve at 3-3.
body: That one point alone provided evidence of the athleticism, explosiveness and sheer audacity that have long marked Fils as such a rare, exciting talent, and it also set the tone for a monumental victory. From that moment onwards, Fils took control of the match and he marched into his first Masters 1000 final at the Cincinnati Open with a supreme performance, defeating Cobolli, the No 7 seed, 6-3, 6-4.

Fils has now reached a final, two semi-finals and two other quarter-finals in his five completed Masters 1000 tournaments this year. He also won his fourth title at the Barcelona Open 500 event and he has won four of his last six matches against top 10 opponents. As he seeks his first Masters 1000, he now sits at No 6 in the race to the ATP Finals. He will rise to a career high ranking of No 11.

articles.title: Enzo Maresca searches for ‘new Rodri’ and expects Manchester City reaction
articles.summary: Maresca: ‘You need to be good at recruiting the next one’ City face Bournemouth after Community Shield defeat. Enzo Maresca has brushed off the loss of Rodri to Barcelona for £65m by stating Manchester City will search for the “new Rodri” in the same way Sergio Agüero was replaced by Erling…
body: Rodri’s departure is a sizable blow to the club’s new manager as he embarks on a first season in charge. Yet the Italian is not fazed by the absence of a player considered one of the world’s best No 6s.

“How do we solve that problem? We try to find the new Rodri, it is what it is. [Before] Rodri arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. He joined the club, then he achieved many important things.

“Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri. I was thinking on Thursday night, when David Silva was here, everyone was worried and Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio [Agüero] was here, everyone was worried [when he was going to leave] and Erling [Haaland] arrived. Fernandinho? Rodri arrived. It is just about this. When they leave, you need to be good at recruiting the next one.
“They are all similar, David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Erling – it is normal, it is change, it is not a problem, go again and try to do the right things.”

articles.title: Highlights! Wint Strangles Chatman For Second Win In 11 Days
articles.summary: Heavyweights Anthony Wint vs. Terrance Chatman squared off earlier tonight (Sat., Aug. 22, 2026) at UFC Sacramento LIVE on Paramount+ from inside the Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, California.
body: The ex-NFL player Wint didn’t waste long in trying to wrestle his larger opponent. Chatman defended a double leg and clinch takedown well, but the single leg transition tripped him to the fence. From his back, Chatman nearly reversed Wint with a kimura. Wint was able to muscle his way free and landed a couple punches from top position. In the final minute of the first, Wint attacked an arm triangle.
The position didn’t appear perfect, but have you seen Wint’s guns?!? After a bit of squeezing, Chatman took a nap.

Two things are clear after this win: Wint is still very raw, and he’s an absolute athletic monster. This pair of back-to-back wins serves to establish Wint as a bona fide prospect. Now that his foot is in the door, hopefully Wint will take some gym time to sharpen his skills before his sophomore UFC appearance. Given a little time to improve, “Bow Down” might turn out to be something special.

articles.title: Stokes stars as Durham thump Derbyshire to lift Championship promotion hopes
articles.summary: Ben Stokes starred again with bat and ball as Durham boosted their Rothesay County Championship promotion hopes with a crushing 338-run win at Derbyshire with a day to spare.
body: The former England captain followed up his half-century and two wickets in the first innings by making an unbeaten 66 before taking 5-17 as Derbyshire were skittled out for 84 while chasing an unlikely 423 for victory.
After resuming their first innings on 127-6, trailing by 156, Derbyshire were all out for 156, with Durham's Matthew Potts finishing with 5-46.
Durham opener Ben McKinney then made a brilliant 140 off 162 deliveries and Will Rhodes made 52 before a 55-ball 66 not out from Stokes saw the visitors declare on 295-6.
Stokes then took three wickets in four balls as Derbyshire's second innings capitulated, with Potts chipping in with 3-22.

articles.title: Dundee claim derby bragging rights with victory over winless Dundee United
articles.summary: Dundee enjoyed another memorable trip across the road as they secured a deserved 2-0 derby victory away to Dundee United to move joint-top of the fledgling Scottish Premiership table.
body: Drey Wright opened the scoring late in the first half before Owen Bevan notched after the break as the Dark Blues made it three wins in their last four visits to Tannadice.

Steven Pressley's side are now level with Celtic and St Mirren on the six-point mark, albeit having played a game more than most of their rivals, after making it two wins from their opening three league matches.
By contrast, United endured a demoralising evening as they went down to a third straight defeat in all competitions to remain second-bottom with just one point from their three Premiership matches.
Terrors boss Jim Goodwin made six changes to the side that lost 4-0 to Celtic in the Premier Sports Cup, including restoring influential left-back Will Ferry after a minor injury.
